item.title: Trump wants a ballroom in Ireland. One man is having a ball fighting it.
item.description: The tiny village of Doonbeg was all in favor of the plan, but concerns about an endangered snail — and “serial objector” Liam Madden — could derail the project.

item.title: Pentagon’s shakeup at Stars and Stripes risks eroding independence of military newspaper, Democrats say
item.description: The longtime Stars and Stripes publisher announced he was stepping away in an email to staff that included a parting shot at the Defense Department. Weeks earlier, an active-duty Navy captain was placed in leadership at the military newspaper, an atypical appointment that staffers, board members and Democratic lawmakers say risks further eroding the publication’s independence from the government.

item.title: Trump says he will pause 50% tariffs on Canada for three days, pending the finalization of a deal
item.description: The steep levies, announced last month, were set to take effect at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday. Just hours before the deadline, the president said that a deal between the two sides was close.

item.title: Republican Rep. Cory Mills, who faces allegations of sexual misconduct and domestic abuse, loses his primary in Florida
item.description: The congressman lost to former news anchor Ryan Elijah in a GOP primary that tested voters’ tolerance of serious controversy. Several prominent Florida Republicans had declined to endorse Mills.

item.title: Reps. Debbie Wasserman Schultz and Jared Moskowitz fend off Democratic primary challengers in redrawn Florida districts
item.description: Wasserman Schultz, a White 11-term lawmaker whose district was cut into pieces by GOP redistricting, faced criticism for running in a neighboring district where Black people make up a plurality of residents. Moskowitz, a moderate, was challenged from the left by democratic socialist Oliver Larkin.

item.title: Trump seeks to open millions of acres of near-pristine national forests to roads
item.description: The Trump administration proposed a repeal of the 2001 roadless rule, raising concerns among environmentalists that already-threatened woodlands could be further fragmented.

item.title: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro set to order new limits on data center development, reversing some of his past policies
item.description: The Democratic governor plans to block the development of such facilities in the state unless they meet certain restrictions on electricity and water usage and receive approval from local authorities.

item.title: Russians pull billions from banks, fearing Kremlin will seize deposits for war
item.description: Russians are withdrawing billions, causing liquidity problems for banks and undermining the Kremlin’s ability to issue bonds to finance the fight in Ukraine.

item.description: The federal judge said it was improper for the Justice Department to usurp the U.S. General Services Administration’s Biden-era decision to relocate the agency to Maryland. The administration wants to move the bureau to the Ronald Reagan Building and International Trade Center in Northwest Washington.

item.title: Kindergarten vaccine exemptions jump to another record high, CDC reports, as Trump and RFK Jr. seek overhaul of immunizations
item.description: The increase in the share of kindergartners with exemptions extends a years-long erosion of childhood immunization rates, and comes as the U.S. battles its worst measles resurgence in 35 years.

item.title: 60 days after Trump signed a deal with Iran, the war is ongoing and the president is stuck in a quagmire
item.description: President Donald Trump signed a memorandum of understanding with Iran in June. The agreement set aside two months for talks to turn the interim truce into a broader settlement, but the window has now closed.

item.title: Actress Hayden Panettiere was in cardiac arrest before she died, coroner’s office in South Carolina says
item.description: The star of the TV shows “Heroes” and “Nashville,” who was 36, released a memoir in May that detailed her life growing up in the public eye, and her struggles with postpartum depression, substance abuse and domestic abuse.

item.title: Supreme Court is asked to hear case on Texas law requiring Ten Commandments in schools, potentially setting up landmark clash
item.description: The justices are expected to decide in coming months whether to take up the case, which is being closely watched as conservatives in Texas and elsewhere work to expand religious rights in public spaces and opponents battle them in court.

item.title: White House races to prepare for new strains of deadly viruses after cutting biosecurity experts
item.description: The Trump administration’s biodefense team has dwindled, and its new safeguards have been delayed — all amid growing concern over AI-enabled pathogens.
